description: JRG Solutions builds real-time environmental monitoring systems integrating satellite and atmospheric data. Our approach to MODIS/VIIRS harmonization uses macro-density patterns rather than pixel-level matching. Full-stack deployment on dedicated infrastructure. Solo team, field-validated.
summary: DEFENSOR JRG is a web-based early-warning operating system that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot data into a unified multi-temporal dashboard. The platform normalizes hotspot counts by density (hotspots per km² per month) to reconcile MODIS's 20-year historical depth with VIIRS's superior 375m sensitivity, producing a single burning-activity calendar with five alert levels from Normal to Emergency. Users can toggle real-time VIIRS, historical MODIS archive, and projected fire layers simultaneously on one map, track planetary fire migration across nine latitudinal bands following ITCZ, ENSO, and IOD oscillations via the FireTide module, and right-click any coordinate to generate a cross-data intelligence report combining fire, weather, ionospheric, and air-quality feeds with brigade deployment protocols. Built with React, Node.js, and Mapbox GL JS, and connected to a mobile app delivering proximity alerts to field operators, DEFENSOR JRG transforms raw satellite detections into actionable wildfire intelligence for emergency responders across South America and beyond.
details:
WHAT IT DOES:
DEFENSOR JRG is a full-stack web application
that ingests, harmonizes, and visualizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire hotspot data
on a single interactive map. The system provides three temporal layers —
historical (MODIS archive, 20+ years), real-time (VIIRS NRT, 375m resolution),
and projected (statistical trend models) — that users can toggle simultaneously
to compare fire activity across time.

HOW IT WORKS:
The harmonization engine normalizes raw
hotspot counts by geographic density (hotspots/km²/month) to account for the
fundamental difference between MODIS (1km pixels, lower sensitivity) and VIIRS
(375m pixels, ~2.5x more detections). This produces a unified Burning Activity
Calendar with five color-coded alert levels: Normal (<60), Vigilance
(60-119), Alert (120-199), Critical (200-299), and Emergency (300+). The
FireTide module models planetary fire migration across nine latitudinal bands,
tracking the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), ENSO, and Indian Ocean
Dipole oscillations to anticipate fire seasons months in advance. A right-click
cross-data analysis panel integrates weather (Open-Meteo), ionospheric
conditions (NOAA SWPC Kp index), air quality (AQI), and nearest-fire proximity
into a single intelligence report with brigade deployment protocols.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT:
- Eliminates the false comparison problem
between MODIS and VIIRS raw counts
- Provides emergency responders with a
single-pane-of-glass view of past, present, and future fire risk
- FireTide anticipates fire seasons 2-3
months before peak activity
- Cross-data analysis reduces decision time
from hours to seconds during active fire events
- Connected mobile app delivers GPS-based
proximity alerts to field operators

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES:
- Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite,
Mapbox GL JS, TailwindCSS
- Backend: Node.js, Express.js, PM2 process
manager
- Data: NASA FIRMS API (MODIS + VIIRS),
Open-Meteo, NOAA SWPC, Copernicus GloFAS
- Infrastructure: Linux VPS, Nginx reverse
proxy, SSL (Let's Encrypt)
- Mobile: React Native (Android APK)

CREATIVITY AND CONSIDERATIONS:
The FireTide concept — visualizing fire as a
planetary wave that migrates with the ITCZ — is a novel approach not found in
existing fire dashboards. The system was designed by a wildfire specialist with
operational experience in Argentina's worst forest fires, ensuring that every
data point translates into actionable field protocols rather than abstract
statistics. Color ramps follow WCAG accessibility guidelines and are
distinguishable under color-vision deficiency.

MOBILE APPLICATION:
DEFENSOR JRG includes a native Android mobile application that extends the dashboard's capabilities to field operators and civilians. The app delivers GPS-based proximity alerts for all active crises — wildfires, floods, severe weather, seismic events, and air quality emergencies — within the user's radius. It integrates the same harmonized NASA MODIS/VIIRS fire data, real-time weather feeds, and ionospheric monitoring as the web dashboard, but optimized for low-bandwidth conditions typical during disaster scenarios. The app was built proactively in response to Argentina's escalating wildfire and flood seasons, and is offered free of charge to citizens and emergency services. It represents the "last mile" of the early-warning chain: the dashboard informs command centers, the mobile app informs the people on the ground.

DEPLOYMENT STATUS:
- Web dashboard: Live at https://defensorjrg.com/dashboard
- Backend infrastructure: 7 microservices running on Linux VPS (Node.js/PM2)
- Mobile app: APK available for Android download at https://defensorjrg.com

 

INTEGRATED HYDROLOGICAL MODULE — GUARDACOSTAS:
DEFENSOR JRG includes a fully operational hydrological early-warning subsystem (elguardacostas.com) that monitors the Paraná River basin across Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina. The system ingests rainfall data from Open-Meteo (6 Brazilian localities), hydrological forecasts from Copernicus GloFAS (UN), and real-time river gauge levels from Argentina's Naval Prefecture (8 stations, Iguazú to Goya). Using the Rational Method (Q = C·P·A / 3.6·Tc) and reservoir balance equations for Itaipú and Yacyretá dams, it projects flood arrival 48-72 hours in advance with a 3-tier alert banner system.

THE FIRE-WATER NEXUS — WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE CHALLENGE:
The hydrological module directly informs the fire module. When river levels drop after a flood event, exposed riverbank vegetation dries rapidly, creating months-long wildfire corridors along the Paraná and Iguazú coasts. By cross-referencing GloFAS drought projections with VIIRS hotspot density, DEFENSOR JRG can predict post-flood fire outbreaks weeks before they ignite. This fire-water nexus — understanding that today's flood is tomorrow's fire — is a dimension of wildfire intelligence that no existing harmonization tool addresses. The system was built in direct response to requests from emergency forces operating during simultaneous flood-and-fire events in Argentina's northeast corridor.

INFRASTRUCTURE:
- 7 PM2 microservices on a single Linux VPS (USD 252/year total operating cost)
- 4 automated data scrapers (rainfall, GloFAS, river levels, GitHub sync)
- Mobile app delivering proximity alerts for both fire and flood events
- All tools offered free of charge to citizens and emergency services
